questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the three basic functions all computers perform?
questions.explanation: The three basic functions in this chapter are input, processing, and output.

questions.prompt: A network interface card (NIC) can function as which of the following?
questions.explanation: A NIC receives input, transmits output, and uses onboard processing to handle network communication.

questions.prompt: Which component interprets and executes instructions in a computer program?
questions.explanation: The central processing unit interprets and executes program instructions.

questions.prompt: What is the primary advantage of a multicore CPU?
options: It uses less electricity than a single-core CPU
It can carry out multiple instructions simultaneously
It eliminates the need for RAM
It replaces the need for a GPU
questions.explanation: Multiple cores let the processor work on multiple instruction streams at the same time.

questions.prompt: Which type of storage is volatile and loses its data when power is turned off?
questions.explanation: RAM requires continuous power to retain its contents.

questions.prompt: How many bytes are in 1 gigabyte when using human-readable decimal notation?
questions.explanation: Decimal notation uses powers of 1,000, so one gigabyte is one billion bytes.

questions.prompt: Which motherboard component controls data transfers between memory, expansion slots, I/O devices, and the CPU?
questions.explanation: The motherboard chipset manages communication and data transfers among major components.

questions.prompt: Which expansion slot type is best suited for a high-performance graphics card?
questions.explanation: Modern high-performance graphics cards use a PCI Express expansion slot.

questions.prompt: What is the time required for a hard drive's read/write heads to move to the correct location on the platter called?
questions.explanation: Seek time measures the movement of the read/write heads to the requested track.

questions.prompt: Which type of storage device has no moving parts and typically uses flash memory?
questions.explanation: An SSD stores data in flash memory and has no mechanical read/write assembly.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of firmware (BIOS/UEFI) when a computer is first powered on?
options: Initialize hardware and begin the boot procedure
questions.explanation: BIOS or UEFI initializes hardware, performs startup checks, and starts the boot process.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct order of the boot procedure?
options: Power applied → CPU starts → POST → OS loaded into RAM → boot devices searched → OS services started
Power applied → CPU starts → POST → boot devices searched → OS loaded into RAM → OS services started
CPU starts → Power applied → POST → boot devices searched → OS services started → OS loaded into RAM
Power applied → POST → CPU starts → OS loaded into RAM → boot devices searched → OS services started
questions.explanation: After power reaches the system, the CPU starts, POST runs, a boot device is found, the OS loads into RAM, and OS services begin.

questions.prompt: Which software component receives data from network protocols and forwards it to the physical NIC for transmission?
questions.explanation: The NIC device driver connects the operating system's network stack to the physical network interface.

questions.prompt: In the layers of network communication, which layer packages the message in a format suitable for the network and sends it to the NIC driver?
questions.explanation: The network protocol layer packages the message and passes it to the NIC driver.

questions.prompt: Which network address is used to get a message to the correct computer on a local network?
questions.explanation: A frame uses the destination MAC address to reach the correct interface on the local network.

questions.prompt: True or False: A keyboard is an example of a component that performs only input functions.
questions.explanation: A keyboard sends input to the computer and does not provide computer output.

questions.prompt: True or False: RAM access time is measured in milliseconds, while hard disk access time is measured in nanoseconds.
questions.explanation: The statement is reversed: RAM is measured in nanoseconds, while hard-drive access is measured in milliseconds.

questions.prompt: True or False: A bus is a collection of wires that carries data from one place to another inside a computer.
questions.explanation: A bus is a shared set of electrical pathways used to carry data and signals.

questions.prompt: True or False: The chipset on a motherboard includes the northbridge and southbridge, which manage data transfers between components.
questions.explanation: In the traditional chipset design, the northbridge and southbridge coordinate transfers among major components.

questions.prompt: True or False: Two computers can communicate using different protocols as long as they both have NICs installed.
questions.explanation: The communicating computers must use compatible network protocols; NICs alone are not enough.

questions.prompt: True or False: A packet contains source and destination MAC addresses.
questions.explanation: Packets contain logical IP addresses; frames contain physical MAC addresses.

questions.prompt: True or False: A frame is created when MAC addresses and an error-checking code are added to a packet.
questions.explanation: At the network interface layer, MAC addressing and error-checking information wrap the packet into a frame.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Internet is an example of a private network.
questions.explanation: The Internet is a public internetwork; an intranet is private.

questions.prompt: True or False: In a peer-to-peer network, centralized servers control all shared resources and user credentials.
questions.explanation: Peer-to-peer networks have no centralized server controlling all resources or credentials.

questions.prompt: True or False: A PAN (Personal Area Network) typically uses Bluetooth technology to connect devices.
questions.explanation: Bluetooth is a common short-range technology for personal area networks.

questions.prompt: Match each term on the left with the correct definition on the right.

pairs.definition: The process of adding headers and trailers to data as it moves down through network layers
The process of removing headers and trailers as data moves up through network layers
A service that translates computer names to IP addresses
A protocol that automatically discovers a computer's MAC address from its IP address
A network limited to a small geographic area like a single building or floor
A network that spans long distances and uses third-party communication providers
A network spanning a city or large geographic region using WAN technologies
A worldwide public internetwork using TCP/IP and other standard protocols
A private network that uses Internet technologies but is accessible only to internal users
A network that allows limited, controlled access to internal resources by outside users

questions.explanation: Each network term describes a distinct process, service, scope, or access model.

questions.prompt: A collection of 8 bits is called a _____.
questions.explanation: Eight bits form one byte.

questions.prompt: The two chips on a motherboard that control data transfers between major components are collectively called the _____.
questions.explanation: The traditional northbridge and southbridge chips together form the motherboard chipset.

questions.prompt: The _____ address is like a “zip code” that gets a message to the correct network, while the _____ address is like a “street address” that gets it to the correct computer.
questions.explanation: IP is the logical network-level address; MAC is the physical local-interface address.

questions.prompt: The command used to test basic network connectivity between two computers is _____.
questions.explanation: The ping command sends echo requests to test whether another host is reachable.

questions.prompt: The Windows server software that provides centralized user account management and security policies is called _____ _____.
questions.explanation: Active Directory provides centralized identity, account, and policy management in Windows domains.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between short-term storage (RAM) and long-term storage. Give two examples of each and describe why insufficient RAM affects performance.
questions.exampleAnswer: RAM is volatile short-term storage used by running programs; examples include DDR4 and DDR5 memory modules. Long-term storage retains data without power; examples include hard disk drives and solid-state drives. With insufficient RAM, the computer relies on much slower disk-based virtual memory, causing noticeable slowdown.
questions.explanation: Include volatility, two examples of each storage type, and the performance effect of paging.

questions.prompt: Describe the four simplified layers of network communication, starting when a user opens a web browser to request a web page.
questions.exampleAnswer: User Application: the user opens a browser and enters a URL. Network Client Software: the browser detects and formats the request. Network Protocol: TCP/IP packages it with source and destination IP addresses to create packets. Network Interface: the NIC driver passes data to the NIC, which adds MAC addresses and error-checking information to create frames and transmit signals.
questions.explanation: Name the user application, network client software, network protocol, and network interface layers in order.

questions.prompt: A six-person real estate office needs to share files and a printer. It has a limited budget, no dedicated IT staff, and employees want control over access to files on their computers. Recommend peer-to-peer or server-based networking and justify your choice with at least two reasons.
questions.exampleAnswer: Recommend a peer-to-peer workgroup. It avoids dedicated server hardware and a server operating system, is inexpensive and simple to set up without IT staff, and lets employees control permissions on their own shared resources. If the office grows beyond roughly ten users, it should consider a server-based model.
questions.explanation: A strong answer selects peer-to-peer and supports it with cost, simplicity, and local-control considerations.

questions.prompt: A company grows from 20 employees in one office to 150 employees across three buildings in different cities. What network type should it migrate to, and what hardware is needed to connect the locations?
questions.exampleAnswer: The company should use a WAN or internetwork design, with a separate LAN at each location. Routers are needed to connect the geographically separated LANs, provide logical separation, and reduce large broadcast domains while allowing communication.
questions.explanation: Identify a WAN or internetwork design and routers as the connecting devices.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between a packet and a frame. What addresses does each contain, and at which communication layer is each created?
questions.exampleAnswer: A packet contains source and destination IP addresses and is created at the network protocol layer. A frame wraps a packet with source and destination MAC addresses plus error-checking information and is created at the network interface layer before transmission as bits.
questions.explanation: Distinguish logical IP addressing in packets from physical MAC addressing and error checking in frames.
